name: Belize

flag.description: A royal blue field with a narrow red stripe along the top and bottom edges and a white disc in the centre holding the coat of arms: two woodcutters beside a mahogany tree, ringed by a wreath of 50 leaves.
flag.symbolism: Blue and red are the colours of the two main political parties, joined in a symbol of unity; the woodcutters and mahogany recall the logging trade, and the 50 leaves mark 1950, when the independence movement began.

hook: Belize puts two woodcutters under a mahogany tree in a white disc on blue, with thin red stripes at the top and bottom.
trivia: Belize is one of very few national flags to show human figures, the two woodcutters in its coat of arms.
The motto on the coat of arms, "Sub Umbra Floreo", means "Under the shade I flourish" in Latin.
The Belize Barrier Reef is the largest barrier reef in the Northern Hemisphere and a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
